title: Standardized Food Insecurity Screening and Referral Protocol
implementation_guidance: Implement a standardized two-question food insecurity screening tool (Hunger Vital Sign) during all routine primary care visits; integrate screening questions into electronic health record templates; document food insecurity status in structured fields; establish clear workflow for positive screens including same-day referrals to food assistance programs; develop partnerships with local food banks and SNAP outreach programs; create resource guide of local food assistance options; provide patients with direct referrals rather than passive information; follow up on referrals within two weeks; track referral outcomes; consider implementing food pharmacy or medically-tailored meal programs for patients with diet-related chronic conditions; rescreen at 6-month intervals or with significant life changes.
expected_outcomes: Increased identification of food insecurity, improved connection to food assistance resources, better management of diet-related chronic conditions, reduced emergency department utilization, improved medication adherence, enhanced patient trust and engagement, reduced healthcare costs.
target_population: All Medicaid-enrolled patients, with particular focus on households with children, older adults, those with chronic health conditions, and individuals living in low-income neighborhoods.
citation: Odoms-Young A, Brown AGM, Agurs-Collins T, Glanz K. Food insecurity, neighborhood food environment, and health disparities: state of the science, research gaps and opportunities. Am J Clin Nutr. 2023;119(3):850-861. doi:10.1016/j.ajcnut.2023.12.019
